title: Box-office holds: seat order, overnight expiry, action routing
scenario: Replay a box-office request log: holds pick the best available seats, expire after 15 minutes, and are confirmed, released or ignored. Test 2 checks sales and request outcomes.

verified.why_correct: It filters to available seats in the section, sorts by (row, number) and refuses partial holds with `len(free) < quantity`. The slice [:quantity] is exact. It is only as good as the types it is given: if number were a string, the sort would be lexicographic, but that would be a loader problem, not this function's.

bugs.title: Seat numbers kept as strings
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_orchestra_holds: R01 gets ORCH-A1, A10, A11, A12 instead of A1-A4, and R02, R04 and R07 shift the same way (e.g. R04 gets A6, A7, A8). Row B and the balcony are unchanged.
bugs.why: With string numbers, best_available's sort is lexicographic, so '10', '11', '12' come before '2'. Only orchestra row A has seats numbered 10+, so only those holds change.
hints: R01 asked for 4 seats in an empty orchestra and got A1, A10, A11, A12. What order were the seats sorted in?
best_available is VERIFIED, so look at what it is given: the type of Seat.number.
probes: Why did the balcony and orchestra row B holds come out right?
Why did sold counts and revenue not change?

bugs.title: Hold age read from timedelta.seconds
bugs.symptom: Test 1 test_balcony_holds: R17 (erin, May 2 18:05) gets BALC-A3/A4 instead of A1/A2, and R22 gets A1/A2 instead of A3/A4. Dora's May 1 18:00 hold was still blocking A1/A2.
bugs.why: timedelta.seconds is only the seconds part after whole days. Dora's hold from 18:00 on May 1 is 1 day 5 minutes old at 18:05 on May 2, but .seconds says 300, so the hold survives and blocks BALC-A1/A2.
hints: R17 (erin) gets BALC-A3/A4 although dora's hold on A1/A2 is from the previous day.
Look at how expire() measures a hold's age.
probes: Why did all the same-day expiries (ben at 09:19) still work?
Why does dora's R21 confirm still come out no_hold?

bugs.title: Release branch condition always true
bugs.symptom: Test 2 test_ignored_requests: the ignored list is [] instead of ['R08', 'R20']. The upgrade and refund requests were handled as releases (outcome noop).
bugs.why: `a == 'release' or 'cancel'` is `(a == 'release') or 'cancel'`, and the non-empty string is truthy, so every action that isn't hold or confirm goes through release. 'upgrade' and 'refund' come out as noop instead of ignored.
hints: R08 (upgrade) and R20 (refund) are not in the ignored list. What outcome did they get?
Look at the branch in handle() that routes release and cancel.
probes: What would have happened if gus or lee had an active hold at the time?
Why didn't hold and confirm requests fall into the release branch?

context_qa.q: In what order are requests handled?
context_qa.a: load_requests parses every row and returns them sorted by ts with Python's stable sort, so equal timestamps keep file order. reports.run then calls Venue.handle on each request in that order.

context_qa.q: What does Venue.handle do before it looks at the action?
context_qa.a: It calls expire(req.ts), which walks a copy of self.holds and frees every hold whose age is at least HOLD_TTL_S (900 seconds), then removes it from self.holds.
It takes seats in the requested section whose status is 'available', sorts them by (seat.row, seat.number), returns None if fewer than quantity remain, and otherwise returns the first quantity seats.

context_qa.q: What are the possible outcomes for a request?
context_qa.a: hold → held, duplicate (customer already has an active hold) or rejected (not enough seats); confirm → confirmed or no_hold; release/cancel → released or noop; anything else → ignored. They are stored in Venue.statuses.

context_qa.q: Where do held_seats and the sales numbers come from?
context_qa.a: Venue._hold records the labels of the picked seats in held_seats under the request id. build_report counts seats whose final status is 'sold', prices them with the PRICES table by tier, and groups by section.

context_qa.q: Why does ben's confirm R05 come out no_hold?
context_qa.a: Ben's hold R02 is at 09:04 and R05 is at 09:19, exactly 900 seconds later. expire runs first with `age >= HOLD_TTL_S`, so the hold is freed before _confirm looks for it.
